title: A zero-differential cohomology model over a field
statement: Let $\kappa$ be a field, $C^\bullet,E^\bullet$ cochain complexes of $\kappa$-vector spaces, and $d:\mathbf Z\to\mathbf N$. Suppose each $H^i(C^\bullet)$ is finite dimensional of dimension $d_i$, each differential of $E^\bullet$ is zero, and $E^i\cong\kappa^{\oplus d_i}$. Then there exists a quasi-isomorphism $E^\bullet\to C^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 0BCC, lemma-lift-pseudo-coherent-from-residue-field; proof checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BCC (current numbering Lemma 15.77.6)

proof.text: The prescribed term isomorphisms give finite dimensionality of $E^i$ and equality of its dimension with that of $H^i(C)$. Choose an isomorphism $e_i:E^i\to H^i(C)$ by equality of finite dimensions (Mathlib FiniteDimensional.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_finrank_eq).

Over a field $E^i$ is projective. Lift $e_i$ through the epimorphism $Z^i(C)\to H^i(C)$ using Projective.factorThru, obtaining $s_i:E^i\to Z^i(C)$. The composites with the cycle inclusions give a chain map: its images are cycles and the source differentials vanish.

For a zero-differential complex, both the cycle inclusion and homology projection are isomorphisms. Naturality of the homology projection and factorThru_comp identify the induced homology map with $e_i$. Hence the chain map is a quasi-isomorphism in every degree.

proof_origin.note: Lean realization of the proof of Stacks Tag 0BCC; the source was read on the official Stacks website. The detailed projectivity, dimension and Nakayama glue is expanded by the worker.
